subject: Archaeology
title: The First Villages: Jericho
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The First Villages: Jericho.

hook.text: Jericho may be the oldest continuously inhabited city on Earth. People have lived there for over 11,000 years.

buildup.text: The earliest settlement had round mud-brick houses and a massive stone tower dating to 8000 BCE — the oldest known monument.

discovery.text: The tower is 28 feet tall and required organized labor. A small farming village built a monument before pyramids.

twist.text: Residents plastered and painted skulls of their dead and displayed them in houses — an ancestor worship practice.

climax.text: Jericho shows that permanent settlement, monumental building, and complex ritual all appeared before pottery was invented.

punchline.text: They built a tower 10,000 years ago. They had not yet invented a clay pot.

quiz.question: What makes Jericho's stone tower remarkable?
options: It is the tallest ancient structure in the Middle East
It is the oldest known tower, built before pottery was invented
It was used as an astronomical observatory

details.summary: Jericho in the Jordan Valley is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited settlements, with evidence of occupation from around 10,000 BCE. Its massive stone tower and wall, built before pottery or metalworking existed, demonstrate surprising architectural ambition in early Neolithic.
details.whyItMatters: Jericho shows that monumental construction predates cities, states, and even pottery. Its early date challenges assumptions about what Neolithic communities could achieve without metals or political centralization.
takeaways: Jericho dates to around 10,000 BCE in the Jordan Valley
Its stone tower and wall predate pottery and metalworking
It was one of the earliest permanent settlements worldwide

faq.question: What is the Tower of Jericho?
faq.answer: A massive stone structure 8.5 meters tall with an internal staircase, built around 8000 BCE. Its purpose is debated — defense, flood protection, ceremonial use, or astronomical observation. Whatever its function, it required organized communal labor at a remarkably early date.

faq.question: Is Jericho the oldest city in the world?
faq.answer: It is one of the oldest continuously inhabited places, but early Jericho was a large village, not a city by most definitions. It lacked the administrative complexity, writing, and large population that define cities. Still, its age and scale are remarkable.
